## FINDINGS

**1. BLOCKER — the two new repository methods do not exist; the code will not compile and fixture mode has nothing to read.**
`RoomRepository` now requires `readEventTail`/`readEventTailHead` (`packages/contracts/src/repository.ts:104-116`), but `FirebaseRoomRepository` (`apps/web/src/repository/FirebaseRoomRepository.ts:106`) and `InMemoryRoomRepository` (`apps/web/src/repository/InMemoryRoomRepository.ts:55`) implement neither (grep finds no definition anywhere). `InMemoryRoomRepository.dispatch` discards `result.envelopes` after filtering `sharedEvents` and stores only `receipts` + `authority` (`InMemoryRoomRepository.ts:170-171`), so fixture mode has no event stream to tail.
*Amendment:* implement both methods; in fixture mode keep `DeliveredEnvelope[]` keyed by destination/sequence.

**2. BLOCKER — `SceneEdited`'s shared copy leaks GM-only unrevealed Threat data.**
`redactedForOthers` spreads `fullEvent` and overrides only `addedThreats` (`templates/eat-the-reich/src/engine.ts:1213-1223`); `updatedThreats` (`rating`/`attack`/`challenge`) and `removedThreatIds` are sent unredacted, and `updatedThreats` can name unrevealed Threats. The projection hides these from players (`engine.ts:1932-1934` filters `isGm || threat.revealed`), so tail replay would hand a player values their projection never shows. `redactThreatsForShared` (`engine.ts:153-155`) proves the intended boundary.
*Amendment:* redact `updatedThreats`/`removedThreatIds` to revealed Threats (or omit unrevealed entries) in the shared copy.

**3. HIGH — bounded 128-id ack list + deferred summary ⇒ eviction re-presents events.**
The design (points 3/5) filters re-read items above the cursor through a 128-entry FIFO. A player's `ActionResolved` summary is acknowledged only on dismissal (`apps/web/src/player2/PlayerDashboardScreen.tsx:247-253`), so it blocks the shared-partition cursor while later events auto-ack. More than 128 later events evict those ids; after dismissal/reload the cursor advances and the evicted ids re-present. `EVENT_TAIL_PAGE_LIMIT=50` (`packages/contracts/src/eventTail.ts:31`) makes 128 reachable in ~3 pages.
*Amendment:* persist the contiguous cursor plus a *bounded unacknowledged-id set* (only deferred items), and advance the cursor immediately for auto-acked items; never key dedupe off an evictable ack list.

**4. HIGH — baseline-at-head hides the member's own recovered `ActionResolved` (regression of findings H/M).**
Reconciliation recovers an accepted command only via `receipt.acceptedSequence`, the *first* emitted sequence (`apps/functions/src/gameCommandAuthority.ts:446`; read-back at `apps/web/src/repository/FirebaseRoomRepository.ts:297-305`). Under design point 4 (ABSENT ⇒ cursor=head, present nothing) and point 8 (queue is the only path), that recovered resolution is never enqueued, so the recovered summary disappears.
*Amendment:* when `reconcilePending` returns an accepted result with `acceptedSequence != null`, seed the queue with the recovered shared event(s) (presentation-only, gated by `result.roomRevision <= projection.roomRevision`), or set the shared cursor to `acceptedSequence-1`.

**5. MEDIUM — "ascending sequence" merge is not guaranteed across partitions.**
Each partition query pages independently (`eventTail.ts:49-55` has `hasMore`); partition A can return sequences 91–100 while B's 51–90 are still unfetched. A naive merge then presents 91 before 60. The stated ordering ("Order: ascending sequence") is violated and theatre cues misorder.
*Amendment:* release only records with `sequence <= min` over partitions of (last-fetched sequence when `hasMore`, else +∞).

**6. MEDIUM — non-own `ActionResolved` re-exposes injury detail the projection withholds.**
Shared `ActionResolved` carries full `injuryMark` (category/boxes/downed) and allocations (`engine.ts:890-908`); for other players the projection exposes only `injuryBoxesMarked` count/downed (`engine.ts:105`) and drops resolved rolls (`engine.ts:1935-1937`). The queue would hold other characters' full payloads in client memory.
*Amendment:* enqueue/redact non-own `ActionResolved` (drop `injuryMark`/allocations) or only enqueue own-character events.

**7. MEDIUM — FIFO-32 `rollId→attackSuccessesRolled` map can evict the viewer's own in-flight roll.**
`ActionRolled` is shared-only and carries `attackSuccessesRolled` (`engine.ts:570-580`); design point 3 caps the map at 32 FIFO. If >32 other `ActionRolled`s interleave before the player's `ActionResolved`, the entry evicts and the Defended line is omitted (the exact "Low" finding L, `apps/web/src/player2/ConfirmSummary2.tsx:54-67`).
*Amendment:* keep the seat's single in-flight rollId entry unconditionally (evict on its resolve/void), not a global FIFO-32.

**8. MEDIUM — multi-tab ledger races.**
One localStorage key shared by two tabs: read-modify-write on cursor/ack loses updates (last-writer-wins), regressing the cursor into replay, and both tabs can present before either persists an ack.
*Amendment:* scope the ledger per tab (tab UUID in key, or sessionStorage) so each tab is an independent surface; optionally suppress the non-focused tab via BroadcastChannel. Document that two open tabs each present.

**9. LOW — revision gate can stall, though it is safe.**
The gate is sufficient (see below), but `getProjection` uses cache-first `getDoc` (`FirebaseRoomRepository.ts:270`), so a stale cached projection holds items until `onSnapshot` catches up; the sync loop's backoff can reach 30s (`useRoomProjection.ts:100-107`). `receive` drops older revisions (`useRoomProjection.ts:67-69`).
*Amendment:* gate against a `projectionRef` and trigger queue release on every projection receipt.

**10. LOW — double-mount/double-present.**
StrictMode runs the effect twice; presentation side effects before ack are not idempotent per eventId in-tab. Two mounts share one ledger and both can fire theatre.
*Amendment:* maintain an in-memory presented-eventId set (ref) as first-line dedupe before any side effect.

**11. LOW — shared `ActionDeclared` still carries `actorMemberId`.**
`redactedForOthers` sets `actorMemberId: ctx.actor.memberId` (`engine.ts:442-447`). `EventTailRecord` correctly omits the envelope `actor` (`eventTail.ts:39-44`), but the payload keeps a member id (same class as `CharacterClaimed.memberId`, so not GM-only).
*Amendment:* strip `actorMemberId` from the shared copy, or document it as non-secret and never render it.

## CONFIRMED-SOUND

- **Partition authorization** matches the design: `shared` for any member, `gm` only for `hasCapability(roomId,"gm")`, `member-{id}` only when it equals the caller's own binding (`firestore.rules`, `events/*` matches). A player cannot read another `member-` partition or `gm`.
- **Shared copies keep the same `eventId`** as private copies: `ActionDeclared` uses `rollId` across gm/member/shared (`engine.ts:455-462`); `SceneLoaded` and `SceneEdited` use one `eventId` for gm+shared (`engine.ts:994-1005`, `1219-1224`).
- **`ActionDeclared` redaction** is otherwise correct: shared gets `stat:"none"`, empty id arrays, `note:null`; full copies only to gm and the actor's own member partition (`engine.ts:434-461`).
- **Revision gate is sufficient in principle:** every accepted command rewrites *every* live binding's projection with `decision.authority.roomRevision` (`apps/functions/src/gameCommandAuthority.ts:466-473`), so a seated viewer's `projection.roomRevision` is monotonic and equals the revision of every event they can tail. Fixture mode recomputes per-viewer projections the same way.
- **Cursor-per-partition** (not a merged number) is the right call for gapped, atomically-committed-but-separately-queried partitions (`eventTail.ts:17-30`).
- **Single-field Firestore queries need no composite index:** `where("sequence",">",n)+orderBy("sequence")+limit` and `orderBy("sequence","desc").limit(1)` are served by the automatic single-field index; the rules' `allow read` covers `list`.
- **`EventTailRecord` omitting `actor`** upholds safety-interrupt anonymity (`event.ts:6-8`); events are presentation-only, projections remain the sole domain state.

## AMENDED-TESTS

1. **tail-authorization** (rules emulator): a player `list` on `events/gm/items` and `events/member-OTHER/items` is denied; own `member-` and `shared` succeed; `readEventTailHead` returns only authorized partitions.
2. **shared-redaction-parity** (property): for every ETR event type and a non-owner player, each shared-payload field is within `project()`'s visible fields; specifically `SceneEdited.shared` contains no unrevealed threat id/stat and non-own `ActionResolved` has no `injuryMark`/allocations.
3. **cursor-no-replay property**: fuzz ack/eviction/pagination/reload sequences; assert no eventId is presented twice and no acknowledged id re-surfaces after ledger reload even when the ack list exceeds its bound.
4. **merge-watermark**: two partitions where one page is full ⇒ released records are globally ascending and bounded by the minimum partition watermark.
5. **baseline-recovered-summary**: ABSENT ledger + `reconcilePending` returning an accepted `ActionResolved` ⇒ the summary is presented (projection-gated) while unrelated pre-head history is not replayed.
6. **revision-gate**: an item is never released until `projection.roomRevision >= item.roomRevision`, including stale-cached-projection-then-listener-catch-up.
7. **multi-tab**: two simulated tabs sharing the key ⇒ no cursor regression, no lost ack, or per-tab isolation, as chosen.
8. **strictmode-idempotence**: double-mount fires theatre exactly once per eventId.
9. **fixture/live parity**: `InMemoryRoomRepository` stores envelopes and `readEventTail`/`readEventTailHead` return the same shape as `FirebaseRoomRepository` for the same fixture sequence.

## DESIGN-VERDICT

**AMEND.** Priority order:
1. Implement `readEventTail`/`readEventTailHead` in both repositories (fixture stores envelopes).
2. Fix `SceneEdited` shared redaction of `updatedThreats`/`removedThreatIds`.
3. Replace the evictable ack-id list with cursor + bounded *unacknowledged*-id set.
4. Seed the queue from reconciled receipts so baseline never hides the member's own recovered resolution.
5. Add the cross-partition watermark to honor ascending order.
6. Redact non-own `ActionResolved` and make the rollId map own-roll-only.
7. Per-tab ledger isolation + in-memory present-idempotence.
